Package com.egradx.notification

Record Class EgradxOutboundMessage

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
com.egradx.notification.EgradxOutboundMessage
Record Components:
organizationId - the tenant this message is sent on behalf of; null for a platform-level message. Decides whose channel configuration sends it
channel - which channel delivers it
notificationKey - the application's name for this kind of message ("order.shipped"), for the delivery log; may be null
content - the rendered subject and body
addresses - where to deliver it, in the channel's own address format — an email address, a phone number, a Slack member id
replyTo - where replies should go, for channels that have the notion; null for the channel configuration's default
attachments - files to attach, for channels that can carry them
model - the template model the content was rendered from, as plain data; null for ready-made content. Kept for channels that send structured messages rather than rendered text — WhatsApp's approved templates
locale - the language the content was rendered in; null for the default
public record EgradxOutboundMessage(UUID organizationId, EgradxChannel channel, String notificationKey, EgradxMessageContent content, List<String> addresses, String replyTo, List<EgradxAttachment> attachments, Map<String,Object> model, Locale locale) extends Record
One outbound message, on one channel, to one or more already-resolved addresses. Each address becomes its own delivery, retried and recorded independently: one bad address in a list of fifty does not hold up, or fail, the other forty-nine.

The channel is always named by the caller. Nothing in this library decides on a caller's behalf that a message should also, or instead, go somewhere else.

Most callers want EgradxMessenger, which builds these from user ids and templates. This is the level beneath it.
